cohort: All hospital deliveries occurring during a 6-month period at a district hospital in rural Nepal.
finding: Cesarean section rate was 18.5%, with meconium-stained liquor being the most common reason, and 12.5% of deliveries were medically induced.
mod_finding: Medically induced labors were less likely to have meconium-stained liquor but had higher odds of emergency cesarean section.
